summary: Concrete light and fog station on Haro Strait, San Juan Island; chosen in 1915-17 and commissioned June 30, 1919. Automated 1962; whale research base since 1985.

structures.note: Commissioner 1919 gives the light tower as 30 feet; archive and Rowlett give 38 feet
Combined light tower and fog-signal building, per the 1919 description
Two one-story dwellings of six rooms each per the 1919 description; archive and Rowlett describe wood houses

access.note: Lime Kiln Point State Park. The state parks page says the lighthouse is open Thursday to Sunday, 12 to 4 p.m., with programs by volunteers from the Friends of Lime Kiln Society.

facts.agency: Washington State Parks (Lime Kiln Point State Park); Friends of Lime Kiln Society (FOLKS) runs the lighthouse programs

events.note: Lighthouse Board first recommends a light on the west side of San Juan Island (LighthouseFriends)
Act of October 22, 1913 appropriates $30,000 for aids in Puget Sound (Commissioner report, FY1919)
Acetylene light established at Lime Kiln, Haro Strait; the permanent station came in 1919
Commissioner's report names Lime Kiln as the best location; the 1915 act carried no appropriation
Act of July 6, 1916 appropriates $40,000 for a light and fog signal at Kellett Bluff or on the west coast of San Juan Island
Site decided: the point known as Lime Kiln, with a fourth-order flashing light and third-order fog signal
Permanent light placed in commission June 30, 1919
Rowlett directory says the present light tower was added in 1938. The 1919 description already gives a concrete tower. Disputed; not confirmed.
Bonneville Power Administration lays a submarine cable from Anacortes; power lines run to the light (LighthouseFriends)
Light automated; chain-link fence with barbed wire built around it (LighthouseFriends)
Declared a state historic site December 15, 1978 and placed on the National Register (LighthouseFriends)
Lighthouse and surrounding sea dedicated as a whale sanctuary and research station under the Whale Museum; fence removed
Friends of Lime Kiln Society (FOLKS) formed to develop educational programs
Centennial of the light station celebrated in June 2019

corrections.why: The permanent light was placed in commission June 30, 1919 (Commissioner, FY1919; Bulletin 1919). An acetylene light marked the point from 1914 (Bulletin 1914, PDF p. 27).

Construction of the concrete tower began August 1918 and the station was commissioned in 1919 (Commissioner FY1919; LighthouseFriends; NRHP says present structures built after 1917). The 1914 date belongs to the acetylene light.

notes_for_editor: 1) Tower height: the 1919 report gives the light tower as 30 feet; the archive gives 38 feet from base to the centre of the lantern; Rowlett gives 38 feet (12 m). The facts use 11.6 m (38 ft); the record's 12.0 m is close to that. 2) Focal height: the archive and Rowlett give 55 feet above mean high water (16.8 m, used in facts); the 1919 report gives the focal plane as 29 feet 7 inches above the ground floor, a different datum; the record's 13.7 m matches no source read. 3) Range: the 1919 report says 'visible approximately 13 miles' with no unit; the record's 17.0 nm is not confirmed by any source read. Not in facts. 4) The 1938 tower claim (Rowlett: 'present light tower was added in 1938') conflicts with the 1919 description and the archive; not used in the story beyond the disputed note. 5) Lens: the 1919 report calls it a fourth-order lens on a mercury float; the archive lists the original optic as 375 mm; LighthouseFriends says a 375-mm drum lens replaced the Fresnel lens. Facts list order 4, status replaced. 6) Dwellings: the 1919 report and NRHP describe reinforced-concrete dwellings built 1919; the archive gives keepers' quarters 1914 and WOOD; Rowlett describes wood houses. Facts use concrete/1919 per the primary report; the conflict is unresolved. 7) Ownership: LighthouseFriends says Coast Guard owns, Washington State Parks manages; Rowlett gives owner as Washington State Parks with a question mark; the 1977 NRHP says the Coast Guard retains only the light and fog-signal building and the oil house. 8) Fog signal: LighthouseFriends says discontinued; Rowlett lists a fog horn every 30 seconds. 9) Name variants: Bulletin index says 'Betteker, Lewis'; LighthouseFriends and archive say Louis. 10) The 1914 acetylene light: the Bulletin 1914 list is OCR-garbled ('Lime Kiln, liaro Strait, Yash., lens lauten:, acetylene'); the evidence quotes are 'Lime Kiln' and 'acetylene' only. Read the page image (PDF p. 27) before publishing the exact wording. The link between the 1913 act's money and the acetylene light is LighthouseFriends' claim alone. 11) LighthouseFriends-only items: the 1908 recommendation, the 1923 Fairplay rescue (no Bulletin entry found in the corpus), the Settles family anecdote, Hermann's later career (Cape Arago, Heceta Head), the 1951 BPA cable and the 375-mm drum lens. 12) No storm, wreck or loss at this light was found in the Commissioner and Bulletin volumes searched (grep for Lime Kiln across 1912-1939 returned construction, illuminant and personnel entries only); the Storms chapter therefore carries only the LighthouseFriends rescue. Newspapers were not searched for this station. 13) Living or recently active people: the archive's post-1960 names (Thomas E. Anderson, Clyde W. Crawford, Louis C. Knight, Robert D. Benson, Gerald L. Nevils, Niles C. Pendleton) are named only as the archive prints them, with years and role. 14) The state parks page is undated; the hours in the story are as the page read on 2026-10-22. 15) Frank DeRoy: a Bulletin 1930 item names a Frank DeRoy, keeper of Warrior Rock Light on Sauvies Island, Oregon. Not linked: a shared name alone is not evidence. 16) The Commissioner FY1918 proposals sentence is cited by scan page (360); the printed page was not read. 17) The Kellett Bluff name: the appropriation acts and the 1919 description use Kellett Bluff; the story uses Kellett Bluff only as the 1915 and 1916 authorisation wording. 18) Photos: none added. Fact-check 2026-10-22: the 1914 Bulletin's 'liaro Strait' is OCR for Haro Strait; the page image was not checked. The dwelling and tower-height disagreements (archive and Rowlett versus the 1919 description, nomination and LighthouseFriends) are now stated in the story.
